newsitem.title: CHINA: China's stock indices end up on interest cut hope.
newsitem.headline: China's stock indices end up on interest cut hope.

text.p: China's A and B share indices all closed higher on Monday fuelled by rumours that a further cut in bank interest rates or in bank reserve requirements is possible later this year, brokers said.
Shanghai's foreign currency B share index rose 1.210 points or 1.96 percent to 62.888 points, while Shenzhen's B index gained 3.01 points or 2.12 percent to end at 145.01 points.

Brokers in Shanghai and Shenzhen said rises in the B share markets were encouraged by gains in their A share counterparts due to expectations of credit-easing measures emerging from a national meeting of bankers which began today in Beijing.
Shanghai's B share market continued last Friday's rebound mainly on speculative buying of selective shares by domestic institutions, Shanghai brokers said.

"Obviously there are some institutions which do not want the market to fall because they hold large positions," one broker said. "But overseas investors are staying on the sidelines, which limits the potential for rises."

Newcomer clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai was again the star, supported by institutions that already hold large quantities of the stock, brokers said. It jumped 10 percent limit-up to $0.356 on volume of 4.8 million shares.
Shenzhen's B share market ended higher boosted by speculative institutional demand for a range of cheap-priced counters, brokers said.
Jiangling Motors, the best performing B share, rose HK$0.23 or 7.77 percent to HK$3.19 and Changan Automobile was the most active share on volume of 2.26 million shares, rising HK$0.10 to HK$4.61.
Shanghai's A share index rose 11.402 points or 1.19 percent to 970.315 points with Shenzhen A share index advancing 9.70 points or 2.88 percent to close at 346.94 points.
In Shanghai, Eastern China Computer A share was the star on speculative buying, soaring 10 percent to its limit-up of 10.12 yuan.
In the Shenzhen A market, retailer Tianjin Leadar closed at its 10 percent limit-up of 6.00 yuan on speculative institutional buying, brokers said.
